newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-INTER STILL CHASING PARMA FOR EUROPEAN CUP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER STILL CHASING PARMA FOR EUROPEAN CUP SPOT.

text.p: Internazionale recovered from losing the UEFA Cup final and manager Roy Hodgson in less than a week to defeat Napoli 3-2 on Sunday and maintain their faint hopes of a place in the European Cup.

But Enrico Chiesa's late goal against Bologna ensured second-placed Parma stay two points clear of Inter and, with one match left, the famous old club is running out of time to enter the Champions' League as runners-up to Juventus.

With Inter fans already making one Englishman -- coach Hodgson -- a scapegoat for their side's UEFA Cup defeat to Schalke, it was ironic that England's Paul Ince should add to their woes in the 31st minute at the San Siro.
The midfielder unwittingly deflected Argentine Roberto Ayala's shot into his own net for an own goal that looked like destroying Inter's European Cup dream.
But the tenacious midfielder made amends with a 50th minute equaliser, volleying home Ivan Zamorano's knockdown.
The Chilean then edged Inter in front before France's Youri Djorkaeff made sure of victory with a third. Napoli's Nicola Caccia scored a late consolation.
Parma were lucky not to find themselves two goals down after Carlo Nervo had a shot cleared off the line by Antonio Benarrivo, and then Marco Schenardi hit the post.
Chiesa took full advantage of the let-offs when he finished off a four-man move with a fierce left-foot shot that squeezed in at Francesco Antonioli's near post.
The result now means Parma need only win at relegated Verona next week to enter Europe's most prestigious club championship for the first time.
Lazio showed Parma the way with a 4-1 home thrashing of second-from-bottom Verona that clinched a UEFA Cup berth.
Giuseppe Signori scored two of Lazio's goals with the others coming from Igor Protti and Roberto Rambaudi.
Fifth-placed Sampdoria also made sure of Europe with a remarkable 4-3 victory at Cagliari, a defeat that threatens to condemn the Sardinian side to serie B.
The visitors took the lead three times through goals from Roberto Mancini, Lorenzo Minotti -- an own goal -- and Vincenzo Montella, following a delightful backheel from Mancini.

But three times the home side, battling for their first division lives, levelled with efforts from Uruguayan Fabian O'Neill -- a minute after Mancini's opener Francesco Cozzo and Giuseppe Pancaro's 78th minute penalty.

But with one minute remaining, and Cagliari down to 10 men after O'Neill's sending-off, Vincenzo Iacopino scored the winner. Sampdoria's hero was promptly sent-off together with Matteo Villa following an off-the-ball clash.
Cagliari's loss allowed Perugia to lift themselves out of the bottom four with a 2-0 home win over Roma, with goals in each half from Milan Rapajc and Marco Negri.

Nevio Scala's side only need avoid defeat in their last match of the season at Piacenza to stay up, although they face that match without goalkeeper Luca Bucci, sent-off in the dying minutes of Sunday's win.
Piacenza's own hopes of staying up took a blow with a 4-0 defeat at Udinese.
Raffaele Sergio, Germany's Oliver Bierhoff, Paolo Poggi and Massimiliano Cappioli scored the goals that gave Udinese a point advantage over Bologna in the fight for the last remaining UEFA Cup place.
Vicenza warmed up for the second leg of the Italian Cup final against Napoli with a 2-0 win over AC Milan.
